_note: The four pilot running rooms.
IGP and LNL are entered in the tender register as several blocks apiece --
Igatpuri as five (LP Ghat, LP Mail, LP Goods, BSL Guard, BB Guard) and
Lonavla as two (Ghat, BVT). Operationally each is one running room under
one contract with one roster, so the pilot merges them: the surviving row
carries the combined beds and rooms, and the absorbed rows are marked
closed with a remark naming the survivor. Nothing is deleted -- the tender
register stays readable.
JNPT is a new running room and is NOT in the tender register. Its figures
below are PROVISIONAL and marked as such on the record itself. Replace
them with the sanctioned particulars when the site is commissioned.
MERGES ARE KEYED ON CODE, NOT NAME, and are re-applied on every run.
A merge renames the survivor, so looking it up by its register name
fails the second time; looking it up by the merged name found a room
that was merged and skipped the work. Between those two, the merge
silently stopped re-applying -- and db/seeds/03 resets total_beds from
the register on every `migrate.js seed`, so IGP quietly went back from
131 beds to 44 and LNL from 72 to 42, with nothing reporting it.
Codes never change. The merge now recomputes from them every time and
says whether anything moved.
survivor_register is the SURVIVOR'S OWN ROW as db/seeds/03 states it.
The merge writes the combined figures into the survivor, so after the
first run the survivor no longer holds its own register value and
re-summing would add the parts to a total that already contains them:
IGP went 44 -> 131 -> 218 on a third run. The absorbed rooms are never
mutated, so only the survivor's figures need restating here. If db/seeds/03
is ever corrected, the loader compares and refuses rather than drifting.

merges.reason: Igatpuri is one running room under one contract; the register lists it by crew type.
blocks_note: THE BUILDINGS AS THEY ACTUALLY ARE, from the officer, 4 September 2026.
The blocks were first derived from the TRO register entries the merge is
made of, which listed Igatpuri as five entries by crew type. The officer
then said plainly: 'change is there. this time my fault. the dashboard
data was stale.' So the register is history and this is the fact.
TM = Train Manager, the post that used to be called Guard. The register's
'BSL Gaurd' and 'BB Gaurd' are superseded in spelling and in name alike.
THE BEDS ARE UNCHANGED AT 131 -- only the composition moved, and the
rooms with it, 25 -> 23. That is why nothing derived from the bed count
had to move: the contract's 107 posts, the band, and the two-days'
washed-stock figure of 2 x 131 all stand exactly as they were.
The seed refuses to write these if they do not total the running room's
own beds, so a stale list cannot pass silently a second time.
female_rooms AND cooks_here ARE STATED HERE, NOT IMPORTED. The inventory
sheet shows the ladies' room as a row of its own, and it would have been
easy to let the importer write female_rooms from it -- which is how the
figure got silently reset to 0 the first time db/seed-pilot.js re-ran
after the import. One fact, one writer: these two are facts about the
building and belong with the building. The importer now CHECKS the sheet
against them and complains if they disagree, rather than writing either.

_division_note: Every pilot site is in Mumbai division. The register also holds an IGP in Bhusaval with 67 beds; matching on name alone would silently pick one of the two, so the loader matches on name AND division and refuses to guess.
